section_title: What had Israel failed to guard in the sanctuary?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 4 Then the man brought me to the front of the temple by way of the north gate. I looked and saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple, and I fell facedown. 5 The LORD said to me: “Son of man, pay attention; look carefully with your eyes and listen closely with your ears to everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD. Take careful note of the entrance to the temple, along with all the exits of the sanctuary.

6 Tell the rebellious house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I have had enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel. 7 In addition to all your other abominations, you brought in foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh to occupy My sanctuary; you defiled My temple when you offered My food—the fat and the blood; you broke My covenant. 8 And you have not kept charge of My holy things, but have appointed others to keep charge of My sanctuary for you.’ 9 This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter My sanctuary—not even a foreigner who lives among the Israelites.

context_lines: At the north approach, Ezekiel again sees the Lord’s glory filling the temple and falls facedown. He is told to pay careful attention to the laws of the house and to who may enter.

The Lord confronts Israel for handing the care of His holy things to foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh. The people had broken His covenant rather than keeping the responsibilities entrusted to them.

The requirement concerns more than residence: living among Israel did not by itself qualify someone for this service. The reference to the heart also makes clear that an outward connection without faithfulness to the Lord was inadequate.
common_interpretation_lines: [Cambridge](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/ezekiel/44.htm) understands the complaint as foreigners being placed in sanctuary service, rather than a ban on foreigners ever presenting offerings to the Lord. It distinguishes people incorporated into Israel’s covenant life from those serving without that commitment.

[Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/44.htm) similarly emphasizes Israel substituting others for themselves instead of keeping the Lord’s charge. The responsibility for this failure rests with the people who were entrusted with the sanctuary.
god_plan_lines: [Ephesians 2:11–22](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/2.htm) describes Gentiles who were once strangers to the covenants being brought near through Christ’s blood. Jews and Gentiles receive access to the Father by one Spirit and become a dwelling place for God.

The wider story therefore reaches beyond being excluded as an outsider. Christ brings people near and makes them members of God’s household. This does not make Ezekiel’s warning about unfaithful service unimportant; it shows where the New Testament locates the way into belonging and access to God.
